To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we propose a Mixed Integer Optimization (MIQCP) approach that explicitly accounts for significance, robustness, sparsity, pairwise collinearities, group sparsity and avoids multicollinearity.

we provide explicit MIO constraints that impose significance and multicollinearities in building linear regression models and we show that our approach has computational advantages compared to Bertsimis and King (2015) in accuracy, computational time and false detection rate

the proposed Mixed Integer Optimization (MIOP) approach to accounting for significance and avoiding multicellinearity in building linear regression models has a significant computational advantage over the cutting plane approach of Bertsimas and KIng (2016).
In summary, our research is concerned with
building linear regression models with desirable statistical properties a priori, namely, significance, robustness, sparsity, pairwise collineary and group sparsity.
the development of a MIO that produces regression models with the desired properties of sparsity, robust, significance and avoiding multicoliinearity.
building regression models that have the following desirable properties: (a) they are sparse, (b) they are robust, (c) they avoid multicollinearities and (d) they are significant
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the MIO approach is the best approach to date in building linear regression models with desirable features a priori.
the MIO approach is superior to the cutting plane framework in terms of accuracy and computational time, and the cutting plane framework is superior in terms of false detection rates.
the MIO framework proposed in this work is superior to the cutting plane framework in Bertsimas-King (2016) when accounting for significance and avoiding multicolinearity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we propose a holistic approach for producing a linear regression model with desirable properties a-priori and we provide computational results that suggest that our approach is superior to existing ones in terms of accuracy, false detection rates, and computational time.

we propose a MIO that produces regression models with desirable statistical properties a priori, and that has a significant computational and accuracy edge compared to the cutting plane approach of Bertsimas and king (2016).
we present a new methodology that explicitly imposes the desirable properties of the model and is computationally superior to Bertsimas-King (2016) for the same purpose.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of explicit MIO constraints for accounting for significance and avoiding multicolinearity is computationally advantageous compared to the use of iteratively imposed cutting plane constraints.
explicit MIO constraints are a powerful tool in building linear regression models with desirable a priori properties.
MIO is the right tool to impose significance and avoid collinearity in building linear regression models.
